20.t: Working with data: peas in a respirometer
q: Calculate the rate of oxygen uptake at 30 °C in mm³ min⁻¹ g⁻¹, after subtracting the boiled-pea reading.
Explain why the drop moves towards the peas.
The peas take in oxygen for aerobic respiration. The CO₂ they release is absorbed by the potassium hydroxide, so the volume of gas falls and the drop is pulled in.
Explain the purpose of the boiled peas and the glass beads.
They are controls: any movement in these tubes is caused by changes in temperature or pressure (or microbes), not by the peas respiring, so it can be subtracted.
Calculate how many times faster the peas respired at 30 °C than at 20 °C. Explain the value.
73 / 38 = 1.9. Respiration is controlled by enzymes: a 10 °C rise roughly doubles the rate of enzyme reactions.
Predict the result at 30 °C if the potassium hydroxide were replaced by water. Explain.
The drop hardly moves: in aerobic respiration of glucose the volume of CO₂ released equals the volume of O₂ taken in.
